analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the "Last updated" date and rewrites the description of NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes. The documented cap goes from 8 MiB to 40 MiB (head lines 128-132). The documented error becomes `media_too_large` for an oversized body, with 400 for an over-context video prompt. A second hunk at about head lines 542-544, outside the supplied excerpt, makes the same change. I could not view that hunk and relied on the patch excerpt only.

This is documentation only, so no code paths or controls change in this diff. The documented 40 MiB limit does affect availability and memory admission (A-001, TB-007, T-029). The units show the surrounding admission design. The ingress reservation is charged before JSON/base64 inspection (head lines 82-83). Media charges are reserved before decode, and `videoMediaChargeBytes` stays below one largest image's charge (head lines 125-127). Requests are capped at one media request at a time per owner, with a 429 for a second. A larger encoded body is therefore still bounded by the ingress reservation and the 503 memory refusal. The supplied evidence shows no missing control.

Open question: the actual code change to `maximumEncodedBodyBytes` and the ingress reservation sizing is not in this batch. Whether the larger limit stays within the ingress charge and whether the transports enforce a matching limit cannot be verified here. The claim that 40 MiB "holds every body the provider's transports deliver" is unverified. A reviewer of the code change should confirm that the ingress charge scales to 40 MiB. No threat-model update is needed from this doc diff alone. T-041 prefix-cache statements appear unchanged and unrelated to this diff.
